# 0077: Published cache lifetime rates are preserved without inventing usage

Status: accepted, 2026-11-09.
Extends [0051](0051-long-context-is-a-tier-priced-per-call-and-records-are-curated.md) with the published 12-hour cache-write rate.

## Context

OpenAI publishes 30-minute and 12-hour cache-write rates for GPT-5.6 and later on the Responses API.
LiteLLM carries the latter as `cache_creation_input_token_cost_above_12hr`, with a separate long-context variant.
The Codex token-usage protocol reports total cache writes without their lifetime split.

## Decision

Store `cache_write_12h` alongside the existing rates in dated records, project overrides and `rates_applied`.
Preserve its long-context rate in the same sub-table as the other long-context rates.
When no rate is published, represent it as absent in the price record and null in the typed applied rates.
Never substitute another lifetime's rate for it.
Keep rejecting unknown cost fields and unknown model shapes.
Recognise the provider's `-law` model configuration suffix, with access eligibility decided in `models.toml`.
Price Codex's untagged writes at the default cache-write rate; do not infer 12-hour usage from a published price.

## Consequences

Curation and live pricing preserve the published lifetime rates through one shared converter.
Historical price records retain their original rates and acquire no inferred lifetime prices.
Exact mixed-lifetime billing requires the capture protocol to expose the write split before an adapter can reconstruct it.
The report's type contract carries the optional rate without changing how its existing cost views calculate or display estimates.

## Lens

Preserve every applicable published rate, but infer no usage category from the presence of its price.
